steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Food choice is influenced by multiple interacting factors: social, economic, cultural, religious, ethical, psychological, and health-related.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social factors include: family meals and traditions, peer pressure, media and advertising, and social status (e.g. eating out as a social activity).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Economic factors include: income level, food prices, availability of affordable fresh produce, and access to shops (food deserts).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cultural factors: different cultures have distinct food traditions, staple foods, flavour preferences, and cooking methods (e.g. rice in Asian cuisine, pasta in Italian cuisine).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name four categories of factors that influence food choice. | Q: What is the difference between Halal and Haram foods in Islam? | Q: What is a food desert?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Social, economic, cultural, religious, ethical, health, psychological, or availability factors (any four). | Halal foods are permitted under Islamic law (e.g. meat slaughtered in the name of Allah). Haram foods are forbidden, including pork, alcohol, and meat not slaughtered according to Halal rules. | An area where people have limited access to affordable, fresh, and nutritious food, often because there are few shops or they are difficult to reach.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When asked about factors affecting food choice, categorise your answer (social, economic, cultural, etc.) rather than giving a random list. Always explain HOW a factor influences choice, not just NAME it — e.g. 'Religious factors influence choice because Muslims will only eat Halal meat' not just 'religion'. For higher marks, show how factors interact — e.g. economic and cultural factors combine when low income restricts access to traditional ingredients. Use real examples to illustrate each factor, especially for cultural and religious dietary laws.
